info.name: 3 · MBA Workshop — Store API (Mock Ecommerce)
info.description:
# Mock Ecommerce Store API

A deterministic, multi-tenant commerce simulator. **Nothing here touches real money** —
payments, shipping and carriers are all simulated.

## Setup

1. Set `SHOP_API` to your deployment (already pointed at the workshop instance).
2. Open `{{SHOP_API}}/admin`, sign in, pick or create a tenant, then **Create API key**.
   The key is shown once, at creation.
3. Paste it into the `SHOP_API_KEY` collection variable.
4. Open **Runner**, select this collection, and run it top to bottom.

Folders 01–07 form one continuous journey: catalogue → cart → checkout → payment →
delivery. Each request captures the ids the next one needs, so a clean run needs no
hand-editing. Folder 08 is self-contained and exercises the failure paths.

## Conventions

- Auth is `X-API-Key`, set once at collection level and inherited everywhere.
- **All money is integer minor units** — `1099` is £10.99. No floats ever touch a price.
- Phone numbers are E.164, including the `+`.
- Country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: `GB`, not `UK`.
- Tax is quoted VAT-inclusive, so `tax_cents` is reported, not added to the total.

## Rate limits

Each tenant allows 120 requests a minute per API key by default, and a full pass of
this collection is about 49 requests. Two back-to-back Runner passes will trip it.
Either wait a minute between runs, or raise **Rate limit per min** under the tenant
config in the admin UI. Every request asserts it was not rate limited, so if you see
a wall of failures, check that first.

## Reproducing a failure

Failure injection is drawn from a per-tenant seeded PRNG, never `Math.random()`, so a
failing run replays exactly. Send an `X-Sim-Nonce` header and reuse it for byte-exact
replay across differing resource ids.

Interactive docs: `{{SHOP_API}}/docs`

request.description: Unauthenticated. Confirms the service is up and reports which database driver it is on — `postgres` when a real database is attached, `pglite` when it is running on the ephemeral in-memory fallback.
The full spec. This is what an agent reads to build its tool definitions. Browsable UI at `{{SHOP_API}}/docs`.

item.description:
Set `SHOP_API` and `SHOP_API_KEY` first.

Issue a key in the admin UI at `{{SHOP_API}}/admin` → pick a tenant → **Create API key**. It is shown once, at creation.

Then hit **Runner** on this collection and run it top to bottom: every folder feeds the next.

item.name: 01 · Catalog

exec: pm.test("found a purchasable variant", () => pm.expect(product, "no in-stock variant").to.exist);

request.description: Captures the first in-stock variant into `PRODUCT_ID` / `VARIANT_ID`. Everything downstream depends on this request.
Full detail for the product captured above, including every variant and its stock level.
Free-text `q` plus price bounds in minor units (pence). Tune `q` to your catalogue preset — try `coffee` for grocery, `laptop` for electronics.
The category tree for this tenant.
Generated from the SKU string alone — no database read, no tenant data — so it is safe unauthenticated and works directly in an `` tag. Set `PRODUCT_SKU` to any SKU, e.g. `FAS-0001`.

item.description: Read-only. Captures `PRODUCT_ID` and `VARIANT_ID` for the cart flow.

item.name: 02 · Customers

request.description: Idempotent on phone number: call it twice and you get the same customer back, not a duplicate or a 409. Returns **201** when it creates one and **200** when it hands back an existing record — so this assertion accepts either.
Lookup by phone or email. The phone must be E.164, including the `+`.
`country` defaults to `GB`. Note it is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code — `GB`, not `UK`.

item.description: Shoppers are keyed by E.164 phone number. Creating one twice returns the same record.

item.name: 03 · Cart

request.description: Attaching `customer_id` is optional — an anonymous cart works too, and can be claimed later at checkout.
Adding the same variant twice increments the existing line rather than creating a second one. Returns **200** with the whole recomputed cart, not 201 — the cart already existed.
Shows the full totals breakdown: subtotal, discount, shipping, tax and total.

Seeded catalogues ship with three demo codes:

- `WELCOME10` — 10% off, no minimum
- `FREESHIP` — free shipping over £30
- `SAVE20` — £20 off over £100

item.description: Totals recompute on every mutation. Prices are minor units (pence) throughout.

item.name: 04 · Shipping and checkout

request.description: Rates come from the tenant config. Anything over the free-shipping threshold (£50 by default) quotes standard delivery at zero.
`ready_to_complete` tells you whether the next call will succeed; `missing` lists what is still required.

exec: // Fresh key per run, reused by the replay request that follows.
pm.test("not a replay on first call", () => pm.expect(j.replayed).to.eql(false));

request.description: Turns the cart into an order. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry cannot double-charge.
Same idempotency key as 04.06. Returns the *same* order with `replayed: true` rather than creating a second one — the behaviour a flaky mobile network makes you care about.

item.description: Quote → select → checkout → order. The completion step is idempotent.

item.name: 05 · Payments

request.description: Returns UK bank details to quote: sort code, 8-digit account number and a payment reference. The sort code sits in the reserved 04-xx-xx test range and cannot move money.
Deliberately **not** scannable — the service never emits anything mistakable for a real payment instrument. It exists so a demo screen has something to show.
The time-travel lever: settles the payment immediately instead of waiting on its expiry clock. Paying an order also decrements stock and creates a shipment.
Omit `amount_cents` to refund the remaining balance in full. A full refund restores stock and moves the order to `refunded`.

item.description:
Nothing here touches real money. Four instruments are modelled, each with a different settlement shape:

| Method | Shape |
|---|---|
| `card` | immediate, may decline |
| `link` | hosted page, settles out of band |
| `bank_transfer` | Faster Payments / Open Banking, 15-minute window |
| `direct_debit` | Bacs, collects in 3 working days |

Only `card`, `link` and `bank_transfer` are enabled by default — tick `direct_debit` in the admin UI to turn it on.

item.name: 06 · Orders and shipments

request.description: The lookup a support agent actually performs. Remember to URL-encode the leading `+` if you build this by hand.

exec: else console.warn("No shipment yet — an order gets one once it is paid.");

request.description: Includes the full tracking history, not just the current status.
Valid states: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`. Omit the body to step to the next one automatically.

item.description: Fulfilment you can fast-forward instead of waiting three days for.

item.name: 07 · Events

request.description: Captures the newest event id into `EVENT_CURSOR` so the next poll can ask only for what it has not seen.
Immediately after 07.01 this is empty — that is the point. Run something else, then come back.

item.description: A polling feed of everything that happened, for building a webhook-free integration.

item.name: 08 · Failure injection

request.description:
Test tokens always produce their configured outcome, whatever the tenant `success_rate`:

| Token | Failure |
|---|---|
| `4000000000000002` | `card_declined` |
| `4000000000009995` | `insufficient_funds` |
| `4000000000000069` | `expired_card` |
| `4000000000000127` | `incorrect_cvc` |
| `4000000000000119` | `processing_error` |

Editable per tenant under **Decline tokens** in the admin UI.
Direct Debit is off by default. The error lists what *is* enabled, so a client can recover without guessing. Enable it in the admin UI and this turns into a pending Bacs collection.
Same order, an ordinary token. Succeeds and settles the order.
Every `/v1` route is behind the tenant plugin, so an unauthenticated call fails the same way everywhere — 401, never a 500.

item.description:
The part a real ecommerce backend cannot give you: reaching a specific failure on purpose.

Self-contained — it builds its own cart and order so it does not disturb the happy path above.

Every draw is seeded from the tenant seed, never `Math.random()`, so a failing run replays byte-for-byte.

item.name: 09 · Cart teardown

request.description: Note the cart from 03 is already converted to an order, so this may 409. That is the correct answer.
A paid order cannot simply be cancelled — expect a 409 here, which is the point. Refund it first (05.05) and cancellation becomes valid.

item.description: Destructive, kept last so the Runner does not pull the rug out from under the flow above.
